sources.citation: Kutsch Lojenga, Constance. 1994. KiBudu: a Bantu language with nine vowels. Africana Linguistica 11: 127-133. doi:10.3406/aflin.1994.948
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.128 gives consonant and nine-vowel inventories and tone marking (H, L, LH rising; fn.2: rising tone correlates with depressor consonants); body is ATR vowel harmony (Ibambi dialect). No mention of stress or accent. (Persee per-page scanned text. the PDF itself is captcha-gated.)

sources.citation: Frieke-Kappers, Claertje. 2007. The Creative Use of Genre Features: Continuity and Change in Patterns of Language Use in Budu, a Bantu Language of Congo (Kinshasa). PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (hdl 1871/11028), 467 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.3 linguistic sketch and Appendix 3.A (pdf pp.136-138 = printed 119-121) treat vowels/ATR harmony, consonants and tone only: 'Budu has High (H) and Low (L) tone. H is realised as rising surface tone (R) if it follows a depressor consonant' (p.121); p.67 'Budu has a tonemic Rising tone (R)'. Explicitly defers tone rules and phonology to Asangama 1983 and Kutsch Lojenga 1994. Full-text search for stress/accent/penultimate/prominence finds no word-stress statement.
